name: Bornean Treepie
rangeDescription: Mountains of borneo
description: Long-tailed corvid of Borneo’s hilly and montane forests; the only treepie in its range. Note stout black bill, black wings with white patch, and warm buffy brown underparts and face.

name: Blue-throated Macaw
rangeDescription: Northern bolivia (llanos de moxos, beni)
description: Large macaw endemic to flooded grasslands of El Beni, Bolivia (Llanos de Moxos). Breeds in cavities in tall palms, and threatened by habitat loss.

name: Sooty Myzomela
rangeDescription: Makira and santa ana (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Silky black with a slight bluish-green tinge to the wing and tail feathers when seen in direct sunlight. Juvenile has a distinctive fleshy yellow bill, tipped black.

name: Cuban Grassquit
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba); introduced isla providéncia
description: A small flocking bird of scrub and grasslands. Note the dark face (black in males and gray in females) that is surrounded by a swirl of yellow from behind each eye, down the sides of the neck, and across the chest.

name: White-lined Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (sandstones of western arnhem land, northern territory)
description: Rather plain medium-sized honeyeater found in sandstone escarpment and gorge country of western Arnhem Land, including the sandstone areas of Kakadu National Park and Katherine Gorge. Upperparts uniformly gray-green, underparts pale with diffuse gray streaks on chest.

name: Yellow-shouldered Amazon
rangeDescription: Coastal northern venezuela including islas margarita and la blanquilla; bonaire
description: Large green parrot of desert Caribbean areas, including mainland. All green with yellow face, yellow shoulder patch, and orange wing patch.

name: Timor Heleia
rangeDescription: Lowlands of western timor (eastern lesser sundas)
description: A rather distinctive small green songbird with a yellow face, a bold black line through the eye, black scalloping on the crown, and streaked light yellow underparts. Juveniles plainer, with little or no streaking on crown and underside.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Bank Myna
rangeDescription: Foothills of eastern pakistan to northern nepal and north-central india
description: Dapper inhabitant of cities, towns, and farmland. Combination of gray body, dark head and wings, and bright orange face and bill are unique.

name: Ratchet-tailed Treepie
rangeDescription: Forest of central laos, northern vietnam, and hainan
description: Bizzare black corvid which would closely resemble a drongo were it not for its jagged chainsaw of a tail. Not as conspicuous as the more well-known Gray and Rufous treepies, which can be common in urban gardens and parks.

name: Black-and-white Warbler
rangeDescription: Canada to gulf states; winters mexico to peru and west indies
description: Distinctive warbler with bold black-and-white stripes over entire body. Adult males have black throat and cheek; females and immatures have white throat and paler cheek.

name: Littoral Rock-Thrush
rangeDescription: Arid littoral of southwestern madagascar
description: Chunky, mid-sized robin-like bird. Males are pale gray and orange, while females are gray-brown.

name: Northern Gannet
rangeDescription: Breeds north atlantic coasts; ranges to coastal northwestern africa
description: Large seabird of the Atlantic with long, pointed bill, wings, and tail. Adults bright white with cream-colored head and black wingtips.

name: Yellow-eared Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Timor (eastern lesser sundas)
description: A small green songbird with a decurved bill, a striking yellow ear patch, a white moustache line, and extensively streaked yellow underparts. Juveniles less well marked below, lacking the yellow ear patch.

name: Slender-tailed Woodstar
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of eastern bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Small, long-tailed hummingbird of NW Argentina and the Bolivian Andes. Prefers humid and semi-humid middle elevation forests, but generally rare and difficult to find throughout its distribution.

name: Mangrove Fantail
rangeDescription: Southeastern new guinea (trans-fly lowlands) and northern australia
description: Small pale gray flycatcher, exclusively coastal and usually observed in or very close to mangroves. Pale gray head and back, white throat and chin, pale wingbars, and a very thin gray chest band.

name: Venezuelan Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal cordillera of northern venezuela (carabobo to distrito federal)
description: Small olive-yellow flycatcher with black ear patch, gray crown, pinkish lower mandible, and bold, contrasting yellowish wing bars. Sexes similar.

name: Seychelles Warbler
rangeDescription: Seychelles islands (cousin, cousine, and aride)
description: A medium-sized yellowish-olive bird with a long tail. A scarce endemic that is restricted to a few granitic islands of the Seychelles, where it is found in scrub, woodland, and mangroves.

name: Helmeted Manakin
rangeDescription: Tableland of interior southern brazil to northeastern bolivia and northeastern paraguay
description: Males are striking with a mostly glossy black body, but with a red forehead, crest, and back. Females are uniformly olive-green and also crested.

name: Smooth-billed Ani
rangeDescription: West indies, southeastern mexico (quintana roo) and costa rica southward to western ecuador and northern argentina, also galapagos (introduced); formerly southeastern usa (florida, where now rare)
description: Anis are bizarre, coal-black cuckoos with long floppy tails and unique, curiously tall, flattened bills. Smooth-billed occurs in a variety of open and semi-open habitats in tropical lowlands and foothills, typically staying low in shrubs and grasses.

name: Pantanal Snipe
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to trinidad, the guianas, brazil, and northern argentina
description: Cryptic shorebird found predominately in lowland wet grasslands and flooded fields. Note the long straight bill, white belly with variegated cryptic plumage, and prominent contrasting pale lines on the face and back.
